about.title: About Us
about.desc:
Formax Racing Team was founded in October 2009. We built the first FSC race car in Guangdong and were among the earliest initiators of the FSC competition, brought together by a group of university students passionate about racing.

We are a university-level research team built jointly by South China University of Technology and its School of Mechanical and Automotive Engineering, with members drawn from mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, business administration and other disciplines. With strong support from the university, the school and society, we independently design and build two brand-new race cars every year — one for Formula Student Electric China, one for Formula Student Autonomous China.

Our mission is to turn engineering practice into a platform for developing innovative talent. “Dare to fight, dare to win, strive for excellence” — we stay with our cars, keep pushing technical limits and accumulate hard-won experience in competition. Over seventeen years, from combustion to electric to driverless, the team has watched generations of students come of age; the sweat is engraved in the honours we are remembered by.

AF24.story: A-Future24 is the fifth-generation driverless Formula Student race car we developed over 12 months. This is a pioneering vehicle. From concept design to final testing, the entire team invested over 5,000 hours of work. As our team's first driverless car featuring a carbon fiber monocoque and dual AMK in-wheel motors, we faced unprecedented challenges during design and manufacturing. Through countless simulations and tests, working day and night, we ultimately developed this stable and precise driverless race car. The most unforgettable moment was during the final high-speed track drive event, when we persevered through sudden heavy rain with team members taking shifts to ensure every system was at its best. Torrential rain could not dampen our passion, and after the storm came the moonlight. This spirit of 'dare to fight, dare to win, strive for excellence' allowed us to defend our national third-place title at the 2024 Formula Student China competition, preserving the A03 car number for the next generation of driverless race cars. Season 24 has concluded; we will forge ahead in Season 25.

AF25.story:
A-Future25 is our sixth-generation driverless formula car, twelve months in the making. As the team’s second driverless car with a carbon monocoque and dual AMK in-wheel motors, we put the emphasis on the autonomous system. Through countless simulations and tests, working late into the night, we finally produced a stable and precise driverless race car.

Yet when we walked confidently into the dynamic events, the car on the track was not the car we had practised with.

In the skidpad the INS drifted strangely and we fell back on offset parameters we had never used before. In the acceleration run we ran into RES interference we had never seen, and AS Ready kept slipping away; on the last — and only — successful run, a Ready timeout meant it did not count.

The one chance to turn the season around was the high-speed tracking event at the end.

Our perception held up under the pressure and completed the mapping lap perfectly. But on the second lap the car began to weave, and we knew at once that it was a control problem. We tuned frantically, and then the problems came one after another — a stop distance we had forgotten to change, a speed profile that suddenly failed… none of which had ever appeared in practice. The clock ran on, and after one slow, safe completion lap we knew there was probably no time to try again.

For everyone there, it was a heavy day. Before it, we had imagined AF25 flying around the track a thousand times; we had not imagined these few hours turning out this way. Compared with the electric car that finished its endurance, what was left here was more red-eyed bitter smiling, more heads held in hands, more bitten lips and self-reproach.

Even with everyone’s eyes red, we still took a national first prize at the 2025 Formula Student China and secured the number A04 for the next driverless car. For Auto-Future, an unsatisfying 2025 season is over. For 2026, we go again.

EF24.story:
E-Future24 is the tenth-generation electric formula car we developed over 12 months.

In the 2022 season the pandemic kept many teams from building a new car at all; we managed to build one in a very tight window, but design flaws put us out with a DNF and nothing to show for it. In 2023, on the strength of that experience, we designed one of the country’s leading four-motor cars — and then dramatically stopped 100 metres before the endurance finish line, failing to finish once again. The hunger to finish an endurance and stand on the podium settled deep into all of us.

Then came the 2024 season: the first in our history in which we designed and built two brand-new cars in a single year. The baton passed from one generation of teammates to the next, and plenty of new ideas came with it. So did the problems: suppliers delivered the wrong parts, and the monocoque came back under-strength because of an equipment failure… Teammates gave up their rest time and improvised fixes; the body and aero group even laid up a second, stronger monocoque. Through all of it, EF-24 raced. Her novel design and high level of completion drew crowds of rival teams, and the all-new aero package was recognized by a judge who had worked as an engineer at Williams F1. On track she did not let the team down: almost every static item passed first time, and she took third place nationally in the endurance.

The team had waited three years for this. Not even that day’s downpour could dampen it: as the car crossed the line and passed re-inspection, teammates hugged and wept, telling each other about the year just gone. Our motto thundered from the podium: “Dare to fight, dare to win, strive for excellence!” Amid joy and regret, the 2024 season closed with a National First Prize. The story of 2024 is over; we are ready for 2025.

EF25.story:
E-Future25 is the eleventh-generation electric formula car we developed over 12 months.

In the 2023 season we designed the team’s first four-motor car, and then dramatically stopped 100 metres before the endurance finish line, unable to complete the race. In 2024 we passed all static inspections quickly, but design flaws kept us from pushing the car to its true limits before the endurance events, and the static presentation threw up problems we had not expected.

Then came the 2025 season. EF25 — or, as we prefer to call it, EF24B: born of a tight budget on one hand and, on the other, of everything we could not settle on track in 2024, it is the answer our teammates gave to their own idea of EF24. A redesigned aero package, a repositioned front suspension, a reworked TVC algorithm… every one of those ideas grew out of lessons from the 2024 season. Through all the challenges, EF-25 raced. Her sheer level of completion drew crowds of rival teams; the judges recognized her too, sending us into the design final and a fourth place, plus the Outstanding Aerodynamics Award. Almost every scrutineering item passed first time, and on the dynamic side she did not let the team down: fifth in autocross, a top starting position for endurance, and third nationally in the endurance itself.

When the car crossed the line and passed re-inspection, teammates hugged and wept, telling each other about the year just gone. Our motto thundered from the podium: “Dare to fight, dare to win, strive for excellence!” Amid joy and regret, the 2025 season closed with a National First Prize. The story of 2025 is over; we are ready for 2026.

EF26.story:
E-Future26 is our twelfth-generation electric formula car, a full year in the making.

In the 2025 season we scored the best result of our four-motor era — fourth overall nationally — and with it earned E-Future26 the number E04. Yet last year’s E-Future25, hero though she was, was also a veteran: we would rather call her EF24B. Her layout and electrical platform descend straight from EF24 — a rear-biased center of gravity, an oversized yaw inertia, and the flaw the four-motor era has carried since its very first year: too much mass. Keep that platform and our dynamic results could never take another step forward.

So E-Future26 made exactly those the first priorities: a low-inertia layout, a compact electrical architecture…

After fighting through a shortage of funding and a monocoque mould that would not cooperate, EF26 emerged. Her design caught up with the thinking of China’s top four-motor teams; the overweight body we had been criticized for was gone — 233 kg, Formax’s first step toward lighter, faster, stronger. The judges recognized it too: we reached the design final again and took fourth place. Two finals in a row — the “static king” of old was finding its form.

Her fate, like her build, was never going to be smooth. Scrutineering came and went quickly. On the dynamic side, the skidpad and the acceleration both set new bests for the four-motor era. Then came autocross — traditionally one of the team’s strongest events — and the car’s electrical system chose that moment to misbehave. 64 seconds was her time, and she set it with only the front motors turning. Even so, she still made the top heat of endurance. We all kept hoping — hoping EF26 would tear up the endurance run and finally show the speed she really had.

Another bucket of cold water before endurance. One rear motor simply would not turn; we pulled the gears out of its reduction box. From the moment the green flag fell, she was no longer whole. Xuan brought her home safely, the driver change came and went, and the TSAL light went green.

Nobody saw the red light come on again. Her race was over.

We will never know how fast EF26 could have gone. But all of us know that EF26 was a fast car.

In the 2027 season she becomes A02, taking the mantle from E34, gaining an autonomous system and going on serving the team. We believe her red light will come on again, and her story will go on being written. SCUT Racing: still daring to fight, still striving for perfection.

AF26.story:
A-Future26 is our seventh-generation driverless formula car, twelve months in the making.

Built on E-Future26's body, she carries every mechanical quality a fast car needs — quick and stable. After all the setup experience A-Future25 accumulated, nobody expected her to be hard to drive — including the autonomous system.

Yet last season's shadow still hangs over this car, and over everyone who built her. “Hefei, a year ago. The driverless car DNF'd in the acceleration, then went into a death wobble in the trackdrive — that failure followed me around for most of a year. Can the car finish? Is it fast enough? What kind of car, and what kind of team, does it actually take?” That is how Zhao Ziqian — AF25's autonomous-system lead and AF26's driverless team captain — puts it.

Nobody was beaten down by that shadow; we turned it into fuel. No idiom really covers the nights spent on code, but commit after commit on GitHub made this car's eyes brighter, her acceleration stronger, her steering freer. In one year we built our own highly customized simulation platforms — two of them, in fact — and a virtual AF25 ran lap after lap inside them; we built a stable speed planner, a complete SLAM and planning stack, a fast and precise MPC… and none of us thought “that's enough.” Everyone understood one thing: to show 100% on track, you have to put in 150%.

“In the end we got an answer we can live with,” Zhao Ziqian adds. “A04 grew up being pulled along by the whole team, and looked after by seniors from several seasons — he is very lucky. All three events performed to expectation and finished cleanly. Thank you all for putting together such a fine piece of work.”

We finally met a stable, fast, intelligent driverless car; we watched her go from yellow to blue in the high-speed tracking event, and watched her step onto the runner-up's podium.

But more importantly, we proved that we have a team that is proactive, united, meticulous and able to execute. That is a spirit worth far more than any award. And we believe the SCUT driverless team will carry it onward, toward the highest step of the podium.
